comparisons.peer_summary: The Company uses the acquisition method of accounting for business combinations, allocating purchase consideration to assets and liabilities based on fair value as of the acquisition date, with any excess recorded as goodwill.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose that business combinations are accounted for using the acquisition method, requiring the allocation of purchase consideration to assets and liabilities based on their respective fair values as of the acquisition date. While Broadcom specifically details the valuation methodology for Intangible Assets (IPR&D) within this framework using the relief-from-royalty method, AMD's disclosure focuses on the general requirement to record excess purchase consideration as goodwill after fair value allocation.

sentences.text: The fair value of IPR&D was determined using the relief-from-royalty method under the income approach.

The acquisition method of accounting requires the Company to allocate the purchase consideration to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed from the acquiree based on their respective fair values as of the acquisition date.
